Taro: I agree that AI can answer questions fast, but the answers are not always correct. Last week my AI tool gave me a wrong date in history, and I almost wrote it in my report. Students must check AI answers against reliable books or teachers. Without that habit, AI can spread mistakes.

[Source A] (a short article)
A teacher named Ms. Olsen wrote about her classroom experiment. For three months, half of her students used an AI tutor for homework, while the other half did not. The AI group finished their homework faster and asked her fewer basic questions. However, Ms. Olsen noticed a problem: when she removed the AI during a test, several students in the AI group struggled to solve problems on their own. She concluded that AI helps with daily practice, but students still need to build skills they can use without it.

[Source B] (results of a school survey of 200 students)
Students were asked what they thought about using AI for study. The percentages of students who agreed with each statement are listed below.
- "AI gives me feedback faster than waiting for a teacher": 81%
- "I sometimes accept AI answers without checking them": 64%
- "AI helps students who cannot pay for a tutor": 70%
- "I worry I think less when I use AI": 58%
- "AI answers are always correct": 22%
question_data.subject: 英語

questions.stem: What is Hana's main point about AI?
choices: AI can replace teachers in the classroom completely.
AI often gives her the wrong grammar explanations.
AI is too expensive for most students to use.
AI gives helpful feedback whenever she needs it.
questions.explanation: 正解は「AI gives helpful feedback whenever she needs it.」。Hana は「it gives feedback at any time」「I can fix small errors immediately」と述べ、いつでも即座にフィードバックが得られる点を最大の利点としている。

questions.stem: Which two students are most concerned about the risks of relying on AI?
choices: Ken and Taro
Hana and Ken
Hana and Mei
Mei and Taro
questions.explanation: 正解は「Ken and Taro」。Ken は「students may stop thinking for themselves」「AI should support learning, not replace the effort」と懸念し、Taro は「the answers are not always correct」「Students must check AI answers」と誤りのリスクを指摘している。Hana と Mei は主に利点を述べている。

questions.stem: Which student would most strongly support the idea that AI makes learning support fairer?
choices: Hana
Ken
Mei
Taro
questions.explanation: 正解は「Mei」。Mei は「AI makes quality learning support fairer, because it reaches students who could never pay for extra lessons」と述べ、費用面での公平性を最も強く主張している。

questions.stem: According to Source A, what did Ms. Olsen conclude from her experiment?
choices: Students who used AI did worse on their daily homework.
Students still need skills they can use without AI.
AI should be banned from all homework activities.
The AI group asked her more basic questions than before.
questions.explanation: 正解は「Students still need skills they can use without AI.」。Source A で Ms. Olsen は「students still need to build skills they can use without it」と結論づけている。AI グループは宿題が速く基本的な質問も少なかったが、AI を外したテストで苦戦した点が根拠。

questions.stem: You want to argue that students should not trust AI answers without checking them. Which result from Source B best supports your argument?
choices: 81% said AI gives feedback faster than waiting for a teacher.
70% said AI helps students who cannot pay for a tutor.
64% said they sometimes accept AI answers without checking them.
22% said AI answers are always correct.
questions.explanation: 正解は「64% said they sometimes accept AI answers without checking them.」。チェックせずに受け入れる生徒が64%という高い数値は、「確認せずに信用すべきでない」という主張の問題の大きさを示す根拠になる。81%や70%は利点に関する数値で、22%は逆に多くの生徒が「常に正しい」とは思っていないことを示すため主張の根拠としては弱い。

question_data.passage:
Your school newspaper club is preparing a special feature titled "Should We Stop Using Single-Use Plastics?" The editor asked five club members to share their views. They also collected two outside sources to add to the page.

**Member Opinions**

Aoi: I think single-use plastics, like straws and shopping bags, should be banned in our town. They are used for only a few minutes but stay in the environment for hundreds of years. If we replace them with paper or cloth, we can cut waste at its source.

Ken: I understand the worry about waste, but I am not sure a full ban is fair. Some people, such as elderly or sick people, depend on plastic straws and pre-cut packaged food for safety and convenience. Instead of banning everything, we should focus on better recycling so that the plastic we use does not become litter.

Mei: For me, the real problem is not plastic itself but our habits. We throw things away too easily. Even if we switch to paper, we will waste paper in the same careless way. What we need is to teach people to reuse and to use less of everything.

Sora: I agree that single-use plastics cause serious harm to oceans and animals, and I believe a ban is the clearest way to change behavior quickly. People act when rules are strict. Asking people to recycle "more carefully" has not worked well so far.

Riku: I think the answer is not one rule but a mix. Bans may help in some cases, but recycling and education matter too. Each town is different, so each should choose the tools that fit its own situation rather than copying one single plan.

**Source A (a short news article)**

Last year, the town of Greenfield introduced a rule that required all cafés and restaurants to stop giving out plastic straws and to charge a small fee for plastic bags. Within six months, the amount of plastic waste collected on local beaches dropped by about 40 percent. Café owners reported that most customers quickly got used to bringing their own bags. However, a few owners said that some elderly customers found the change difficult, and they hoped the town would offer paper straws for free to those who needed them.

**Source B (a survey of 300 town residents)**

Residents were asked which action they thought would best reduce plastic waste. Each person chose only one option.

- Banning single-use plastics: 38%
- Improving recycling systems: 27%
- Teaching people to reuse and use less: 30%
- No action is needed: 5%

Residents were also asked whether they already bring their own shopping bag when buying food.

- Always: 52%
- Sometimes: 33%
- Never: 15%
question_data.subject: 英語

questions.stem: Which statement best summarizes Ken's opinion?
choices: Single-use plastics should be banned everywhere as soon as possible.
Each town should freely choose its own mix of solutions.
The main problem is wasteful habits rather than plastic itself.
A complete ban could be unfair to some people, so improving recycling is a better choice.
questions.explanation: 正解は「A complete ban could be unfair to some people, so improving recycling is a better choice.」。Kenは「I am not sure a full ban is fair」「Some people, such as elderly or sick people, depend on plastic straws」と述べ、全面禁止は一部の人に不公平だとし、「we should focus on better recycling」とリサイクル改善を提案している。

questions.stem: Which two members most clearly support banning single-use plastics?
choices: Aoi and Sora
Ken and Mei
Mei and Riku
Ken and Riku
questions.explanation: 正解は「Aoi and Sora」。Aoiは「single-use plastics ... should be banned in our town」と明言し、Soraも「I believe a ban is the clearest way to change behavior quickly」と禁止を支持している。一方Kenは禁止に懐疑的、Meiは習慣が問題だとし、Rikuは一つの規則でなく組合せを主張するため、禁止支持として最も明確なのはAoiとSora。

questions.stem: Whose opinion is best supported by the results reported in Source A?
choices: Mei, because paper is wasted as easily as plastic
Sora, because a strict rule quickly changed people's behavior
Riku, because every town should copy Greenfield's plan
Ken, because recycling alone removed all beach litter
questions.explanation: 正解は「Sora, because a strict rule quickly changed people's behavior」。Soraは「People act when rules are strict」と述べる。Source AではGreenfieldが厳しい規則を導入し「six months」で浜のプラごみが「about 40 percent」減り、客もすぐに適応したと報告されており、厳しい規則が行動を素早く変えたとするSoraの意見を裏づける。

questions.stem: According to Source A, what did a few café owners hope the town would do?
choices: Ban paper straws as well as plastic straws
Stop charging any fee for plastic bags
Provide paper straws for free to customers who needed them
Increase the fee for plastic bags every month
questions.explanation: 正解は「Provide paper straws for free to customers who needed them」。Source Aに「they hoped the town would offer paper straws for free to those who needed them」とあり、高齢の客が変化に苦労したことを受けて、必要な人に紙ストローを無料で提供することを望んだと述べられている。

question_data.passage:
Your high school English class is preparing a short essay project about whether companies should allow remote work. Five students shared their opinions, and you also read two sources to support your writing.

[Students' Opinions]

Mika: I think remote work is a great choice for many people. Workers can save the time they used to spend traveling to the office, and they can use that time for sleep or family. People who live far from cities can also keep good jobs without moving. For me, freedom to choose where I work is the most important benefit.

Ken: I agree that saving travel time is useful, but I worry about young workers. When new staff cannot meet their seniors face to face, they learn skills more slowly. Companies should bring everyone to the office at least a few days each week so that experienced workers can teach beginners directly.

Sara: My main concern is the feeling of being alone. When I imagine working from home every day, I picture a quiet room with no one to talk to. Chatting with co-workers makes the day enjoyable, and a friendly office keeps workers happy. Without that, people may feel sad even if the work itself is easy.

Daniel: I believe companies should decide based on the type of job. Some tasks, such as writing reports or designing software, can be done well from anywhere. Other tasks, such as helping customers in a shop, must be done in person. A single rule for all workers does not make sense to me.

Lina: For me, the planet matters most. When people stay home, fewer cars and trains are used, so less harmful gas is released into the air. If many companies allow remote work, our cities could become cleaner and healthier. This is a benefit that helps everyone, not just the workers themselves.

[Source A] (a short article)

A recent report studied how remote work affects new employees. It found that beginners who worked only from home took about 30% longer to reach the same skill level as those who came to the office regularly. The report explained that beginners often learn best by watching experienced workers closely and asking quick questions in person. However, the same report noted that experienced workers usually performed just as well at home as in the office. The authors concluded that a mixed style, with some office days for training, may help new staff most.

[Source B] (survey data)

A survey asked 1,000 office workers what they liked or disliked about remote work. The results below show the percentage of workers who chose each answer.

- "I save commuting time": 81%
- "I feel lonely at home": 46%
- "I can focus better at home": 58%
- "I miss talking with co-workers": 52%
- "My work and home life mix too much": 39%

The survey also found that 67% of all workers wanted a mixed style, working some days at home and some days at the office, rather than choosing only one.
question_data.subject: 英語

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes Mika's main opinion?
choices: Companies should require all workers to come to the office every day.
Remote work harms the environment and should be limited.
New workers cannot learn skills properly when working from home.
The most valuable point of remote work is being free to choose one's workplace.
questions.explanation: 正解は「The most valuable point of remote work is being free to choose one's workplace.」。Mikaは通勤時間の節約や遠方在住者の利点を挙げた上で、最後に「freedom to choose where I work is the most important benefit」と述べており、働く場所を選べる自由を最重要と考えている。

questions.stem: Which opinion is shared by both Ken and Source A?
choices: Beginners learn skills better with some in-person time at the office.
All jobs can be done equally well from any location.
Experienced workers perform worse when they work from home.
Remote work mainly helps protect the environment.
questions.explanation: 正解は「Beginners learn skills better with some in-person time at the office.」。Kenはyoung workersが対面でないと学びが遅いとし、オフィス勤務日を設けて先輩が直接教えるべきだと述べる。Source Aも在宅のみの初心者は習熟に約30%長くかかり、対面での訓練日を含む混合スタイルが最も役立つと結論しており、両者は一致する。

questions.stem: If a writer wanted to argue that remote work benefits society as a whole rather than only individual workers, whose opinions would most strongly support that view?
choices: Mika and Sara
Lina and Mika
Sara and Ken
Ken and Daniel
questions.explanation: 正解は「Lina and Mika」。Linaは在宅で車や電車の利用が減り有害な排気が減って都市が清潔になる、これは「helps everyone, not just the workers themselves」と社会全体の利益を述べる。Mikaも遠方の人が引っ越さずに良い仕事を保てるなど広く人々に及ぶ利点を挙げており、社会全体への利益を支持する立場として最も適切。SaraとKenは職場内の問題に焦点を当てている。

questions.stem: According to Source A, which statement is correct?
choices: Experienced workers performed much worse when working from home.
The report recommended that everyone work fully from home.
Beginners who worked only from home took about 30% longer to reach the same skill level.
New employees learned fastest when they never visited the office.
questions.explanation: 正解は「Beginners who worked only from home took about 30% longer to reach the same skill level.」。Source Aは在宅のみの初心者が「about 30% longer to reach the same skill level」と明記し、経験者は在宅でも同等の成果を出したとも述べている。よって経験者が大幅に悪化したとする選択肢や全員在宅推奨は誤り。

questions.stem: Based on the data in Source B, which conclusion is best supported?
choices: More than half of the workers felt lonely while working at home.
Saving commuting time was the least common reason chosen by workers.
Most workers said they could not focus when working at home.
A large majority of workers preferred a mixed style over choosing only one location.
questions.explanation: 正解は「A large majority of workers preferred a mixed style over choosing only one location.」。Source Bは67%が一方だけでなく在宅とオフィスを組み合わせる混合スタイルを望んだと示しており、これは大多数にあたる。一方「lonely」は46%で半数未満、「focus better at home」は58%で多数が集中できると答えており、commuting time節約は81%で最多。よって他の選択肢は数値と矛盾する。

question_data.passage:
Your English club is preparing a short essay project about tourism and local culture. Your group collected five members' opinions and two sources. Read them and answer the questions.

[Members' Opinions]

Hana: Tourism brings money and jobs to small towns. In my hometown, an old fishing village near the sea was losing young people every year. After it became a popular spot for visitors, several restaurants and guesthouses opened, and some young families moved back to run them. I believe tourism can keep a local community alive when it would otherwise disappear.

Ken: I worry about what tourism does to daily life. When too many visitors come, streets get crowded, rents rise, and shops that local people need are replaced by souvenir stores. The town may earn money, but residents lose the quiet, ordinary life they used to enjoy. We should ask whether the income is worth that cost.

Mei: I think the real danger is to culture itself. Traditional festivals and crafts can become simple shows performed only to please tourists. When a dance that once had deep meaning is repeated many times a day for photographs, it slowly loses its true spirit. Money should not turn living culture into a product.

Riku: I disagree that tourism harms culture. In fact, attention from visitors often gives local people a new reason to protect their traditions. When outsiders admire a craft or festival, young residents feel proud and decide to learn it instead of letting it die. Tourism can be a tool for keeping culture alive, not destroying it.

Sana: I believe the key is how a town manages its visitors. Tourism is neither purely good nor purely bad; the result depends on planning. A town that limits visitor numbers and shares income fairly can enjoy the benefits while avoiding the worst problems. Without rules, even a small town can be damaged.

[Source A]
A travel magazine reported on a mountain village that became famous online. In one summer, the number of visitors grew so large that local buses were always full, and residents could not get to the hospital easily. The village council responded by introducing a reservation system: only a fixed number of visitors are allowed each day, and part of the entrance fee is used to repair old houses and support local craftspeople. After the change, residents said daily life became calmer, and several young people began training under traditional craft masters again.

[Source B]
A survey asked 500 residents of tourist towns whether they felt tourism had a positive effect on different parts of local life. The percentage who answered "positive" was as follows.
- Job opportunities: 78%
- Town income: 72%
- Preserving traditional culture: 41%
- Quietness of daily life: 23%
- Cost of housing: 19%
question_data.subject: 英語

questions.stem: What is Mei's main opinion about tourism?
choices: Tourism can turn meaningful traditions into shows that lose their true spirit.
Tourism is the best way to bring money and jobs to small towns.
Tourism gives young residents a new reason to protect their culture.
Tourism is harmful only when a town fails to plan for visitors.
questions.explanation: 正解は「Tourism can turn meaningful traditions into shows that lose their true spirit.」。Meiは「Traditional festivals and crafts can become simple shows performed only to please tourists」「a dance that once had deep meaning ... slowly loses its true spirit」と述べ、文化が単なる見世物・商品に変わる危険を主張している。

questions.stem: Which opinion do Hana and Riku share?
choices: Tourism damages the quiet daily life of residents.
Tourism can have a positive effect on a local community.
Tourism should be controlled by strict rules and planning.
Tourism turns traditional culture into a product for sale.
questions.explanation: 正解は「Tourism can have a positive effect on a local community.」。Hanaは「tourism can keep a local community alive」と地域維持の効果を、Rikuは「Tourism can be a tool for keeping culture alive」と文化維持の効果を述べ、ともに観光の前向きな効果を認めている。

questions.stem: Which two members would most likely agree that tourism needs careful management or limits to avoid harming residents?
choices: Hana and Riku
Hana and Mei
Ken and Sana
Riku and Sana
questions.explanation: 正解は「Ken and Sana」。Kenは過剰な観光客が住民の生活を奪う問題を挙げ income が見合うか問うべきだとし、Sanaは「A town that limits visitor numbers and shares income fairly」と管理・制限の必要を述べる。両者とも管理・制限で住民被害を防ぐ立場である。

questions.stem: According to Source A, what did the village council do in response to the problem?
choices: It built a new hospital so residents could get medical care easily.
It banned all visitors from entering the village in summer.
It increased the number of local buses to carry more visitors.
It set a daily limit on visitors and used fees to repair houses and support craftspeople.
questions.explanation: 正解は「It set a daily limit on visitors and used fees to repair houses and support craftspeople.」。Source Aに「introducing a reservation system: only a fixed number of visitors are allowed each day, and part of the entrance fee is used to repair old houses and support local craftspeople」とある。

questions.stem: Which statement is best supported by the data in Source B?
choices: Residents felt tourism had a more positive effect on job opportunities than on the quietness of daily life.
More residents saw a positive effect on housing costs than on town income.
Most residents felt tourism positively preserved traditional culture.
Residents rated the quietness of daily life as the most positive effect of tourism.
questions.explanation: 正解は「Residents felt tourism had a more positive effect on job opportunities than on the quietness of daily life.」。Source Bでは Job opportunities が78%、Quietness of daily life が23%で、雇用の方が肯定評価が高い。Town income(72%)>Cost of housing(19%)、文化保存は41%で過半数に届かず、静けさは最低水準なので他は誤り。
